messages:
alex: Quick thread — thinking about where the feature flags and client shim logic should live for hosted/dedicated/private. Two patterns on the table: (A) fat client + thin control plane (client decides fallbacks, flags) or (B) thin client + control-plane-driven flags and routing. tradeoffs?

mira: +1 need to consider on-prem (private) constraints — metadata and secret access vary a lot there.

tj: tl;dr: control plane gives central visibility and easier rollout, but increases coupling for private installs.

sanju: If we push decisions to control plane we need a probe-first handshake to validate capabilities before routing. otherwise private could break on install.

alex: Exactly. Probe-first handshake idea: client pings local shim with capability manifest, control plane caches snapshot. If mismatch, control plane returns a compatibility policy (fallback model, quantization level, deny). Thoughts on policy shape?

eva: policy should be simple: allow|warn|deny + fallback target + max_seq_len + qos_hint. Keep it compact for air-gapped installs.

mira: For hosted we can be greedy with flags (A/B, ramp %, time windows). For private, prefer declarative pins shipped in the manifest. Ops can opt into remote flags but default to manifest.

tj: Ops/telemetry question: who emits telemetry about flag-driven fallbacks? Client or control plane? We need token-level cost attribution when fallback happens.

sanju: emit from client shim with a signed event to control plane (or local sink) so private customers keep provenance. minimize PII.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout 10% of requests -> control-plane-flag "quantize_beta" enabled for hosted cluster r3.queued (timestamp 4821234579)

alex: Nice. Also thinking about circuit breakers: client should have a local circuit that triggers after X 5xxs or latency p95>threshold and immediately route to fallback variant without roundtrip. Control plane can update thresholds but client must be able to act offline.

eva: +1. offline behavior matters for private. Also provide deterministic order: probe -> capability manifest -> control-plane policy (if available) -> local circuit decisions.

mira: Secret propagation: private installs often lack central KMS access. We should support secret binding in manifest (base64-encrypted) and a short-lived rebind token for hosted to rotate. Don't allow control plane to request secrets.

tj: SDK ergonomics: expose two layers: Redwood.Client (high-level routing + policy handling) and Redwood.RuntimeShim (low-level connection + probe API). Keep the high-level defaults opinionated.

sanju: Rollout playbook: when introducing a control-plane flag that affects latency/cost, require: param docs, telemetry points (client shim emits event), canary percentage, emergency-off circuit.

alex: Quick proposal to decide on today: default pattern = thin client (routing + local CB + probe) + control-plane flags as advisory (not required) for private; hosted gets full control-plane flags with rollout primitives. If we agree I'll draft RFC with manifest and probe schema.

mira: I can take manifest schema draft. will include secrets section and versioning.

eva: I'll stub the shim API examples and the telemetry event shapes.

tj: I'll write the rollout checklist and emergency-off patterns.

sanju: I'll write the compatibility probe flow and state machine for offline behavior.

alex: thanks team. small follow up: do we want a single boolean "control-authoritative" in manifest to let private opt into control plane taking precedence?

mira: yes, make it explicit and default false. that makes upgrades predictable.

eva: add a TTL field for cached control-plane policy so we know when to re-probe.

tj: agree. TTL + priority order solves most race cases.

alex: OK will file RFC and link to this thread. marking this resolved for design sync scope. :white_check_mark:
